findings.summary: zip: Critical Parser Differential & Security Control Bypass via Dual-Header Inconsistencies (Zip Cloaking) Leading to Arbitrary File Overwrite & RCE
ZipStreamReader::extract() and ZipArchive::extract() apply Unix permissions through symlinks without confining the target

evidence: the project's source does not use ZipStreamReader::extract, ZipArchive::extract, but other packages depend on zip

findings.summary: gitoxide: CommandForbiddenInModulesConfiguration Bypass in gix_submodule::File::update() Enables Arbitrary Command Execution via .gitmodules

evidence: named only in files that do not import gix

findings.summary: gix and gitoxide: unvalidated submodule name traverses out of .git/modules and redirects state() / open() to another repository
gix's submodule name validation bypass + trust inheritance flaw enables path traversal and credential disclosure
gix and gitoxide's symlinked .gitmodules are followed and parsed from outside of the repository
gix-fs: Symlink prefix-reuse allows worktree escape during checkout
gix-pack has multiple DoS vectors: unchecked indexing panics and uncapped OOM allocations from crafted pack data
hickory-proto: NSEC3 closest-encloser proof validation enters unbounded loop on cross-zone responses
NSEC3 owner names not checked against the zone in DNSSEC validation (hickory-proto)
hickory-resolver: Resolver::lookup() and Resolver::lookup_ip() APIs obscure DNSSEC validation failures

evidence: the project's source does not use Resolver::lookup, Resolver::lookup_ip, but other packages depend on hickory-resolver

findings.summary: Peer minimum ACK delay can panic quinn-proto when ACK_FREQUENCY transmission is enabled

evidence: the project's source does not use ACK_FREQUENCY, but other packages depend on quinn-proto

findings.summary: Outgoing datagram buffer accounting can panic the sender in quinn-proto
